text.p: NGC Corp and NOVA Corp said Wednesday they reached an agreement-in-principle to restructure their Canadian natural gas operations.
The two companies jointly own Novagas Clearinghouse (NCL), based in Calgary, with NGC holding 49.9 percent and NOVA holding 50.1 percent.
The companies said the move will allow them both to pursue respective core businesses in Canada more effectively.
The new organization is expected to be effective within the first quarter of 1997.

NGC will control NCL's gas and gas-liquids marketing business. NGC and NOVA will undertake separate midstream asset businesses in Canada, with NOVA assuming full ownership of NCL's existing gathering and processing business, the companies said in a released statement.
NOVA will own 100 percent of Pan-Alberta Gas Ltd, which is now a subsidiary of NCL. NGC will operate its new Canadian operations under the name NGC Canada Inc.

"This agreement allows NGC to merge our crude and electric businesses with our gas and gas liquids marketing operations to replicate our Energy Store in Canada, providing the same energy products and services across the border that we provide in the United States," NGC Chairman and Chief Executive Chuck Watson said in the release.
Through the reorganization, NGC's Canadian operation will be structured identically to the U.S. operation. Divisions of NGC Canada, Inc. will be:
- Natural Gas Clearinghouse - Canada -- gas marketing;
- Warren Petroleum Limited Partnership - Canada -- gas gathering, processing and gas liquids marketing;
- NGC Oil Trading and Transportation (NOTTI) - Canada -- crude oil marketing.
NOVA first acquired an interest in NGC in January 1994. The two companies formed NCL as a joint venture one month later.
On August 31, NGC completed a merger with Chevron's gas and liquids marketing businesses.
